cleanIntro: The CZ 457's field strip is three steps: magazine out, safety off, bolt catch pressed and the bolt drawn out. What makes this rimfire worth reading about rather than just doing is the modular system — the barrel is a swappable unit shared with the CZ 455, the stock screws have a stated torque you are asked to check at every clean, and a MATCH-chambered version will not take just any .22 LR. Everything below is read off the English section of CZ's CZ 457 manual, PDF pages 2 to 14.

steps.title: Know which 457 you have — a MATCH chamber is not a general-purpose one
steps.action: Before loading or cleaning, establish whether your rifle is a .22 LR MATCH-chambered version such as the CZ 457 Varmint MTR. Those chambers are cut to the minimum the CIP standard allows in order to improve accuracy, and non-standard ammunition — high power, longer case, longer range — is not recommended in them.
steps.prose: This is a real dimensional limit, not a marketing preference: a chamber reduced to the bottom of tolerance will not accept a case that a standard chamber swallows without comment. CZ's own warning is that using non-standard ammunition in one may cause faulty operation or damage the firearm. It matters at cleaning time too, because a MATCH chamber fouls tighter and a chamber brush that is fine on a standard 457 needs a lighter hand here. If you do not know which yours is, the barrel marking and the model designation are where to look.
steps.caution: Using non-standard ammunition may cause faulty operation or damage the firearm. CZ also says it does not recommend frequent dry firing of this rifle; use snap caps for dry practice.
steps.quote: For CZ 457 cal .22 LR MATCH models (e.g. version CZ 457 Varmint MTR) Match ammunition is recommended for best firing accuracy.
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Ammunition, p.6

steps.title: The barrel and magazine are shared with the CZ 455 — and only those
steps.action: If barrels or magazines are being swapped, note what actually interchanges: CZ states the CZ 457's barrels and magazines share the same interface as the CZ 455. That is a parts-fit statement, not a licence to treat the two rifles as the same gun.
steps.prose: The 457 is built around a modular system that allows barrel replacement and calibre change at user level, and the 455 shares the interface — but the two rifles differ where it counts for handling, including a striker roughly two thirds lighter on the 457, which is why it kicks the sights around less. The controls differ too: CZ's own mini-set leaflet has you depress the TRIGGER to remove a 455's bolt and the BOLT CATCH to remove a 457's. A 455 procedure read onto a 457 will send you pulling a trigger on a rifle you have not finished clearing.
steps.aside: CZ's own caution on barrel swapping is that each exchangeable barrel supplied in a mini-set must be fitted individually by a gunsmith before its first use — fitting a barrel is not part of routine cleaning.
steps.quote: Barrels and magazines are compatible with the CZ 455 (same interface)
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Description and Terminology — characteristic features, p.5

steps.title: Magazine — or single-shot adapter — out first
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction. Press the magazine catch at the FRONT of the magazine in a rearward direction and remove the magazine, or the single-shot adapter if one is fitted, from the rifle.
steps.prose: The catch is at the front of the magazine and it is pressed backwards, which is the opposite of what most bolt rifles teach the thumb to do — expect to look for it the first time. If a single-shot adapter is fitted, it is what comes out here, and its presence tells you the rifle was set up for accuracy work rather than field use. CZ makes this the first numbered step of the strip, before the safety is touched.
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 1, p.10

steps.title: Open the bolt, check the chamber, read the cocking indicator
steps.action: Open the bolt and check that the cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected. Look into the chamber. Then close the bolt and dry-fire only if the chamber has been confirmed empty.
steps.prose: The 457's cocking indicator gives you a second, independent reading: when the striker is cocked its rear part protrudes over the plug and you can check it by sight or by touch. That is not a substitute for looking into the chamber — a rimfire will happily leave a round in the raceway — but a protruding indicator on a rifle you thought you had dry-fired is worth stopping for. CZ's own unloading sequence closes with a trigger press, and it puts a note beside it that frequent dry firing is not recommended.
steps.quote: Open the bolt and check to ensure that the cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Unloading of the Rifle, p.7
steps.warn: The CZ 457 can have its bolt withdrawn with the safety still engaged, which CZ lists as a feature for safe handling when unloading. Use it — the safety does not have to come off to check the chamber.

steps.title: Safety to Off so the bolt will come out
steps.action: Shift the safety to its "Off" position. On the 457 the safety is pushed backward to "Safety-On", uncovering a white dot; forward is off, and it must be off for the bolt to be withdrawn from the receiver.
steps.prose: There is a genuine subtlety here worth holding onto: the 457 lets you pull the bolt back WITH the safety on, which is how you check a chamber safely, but CZ's strip step calls for the safety off before the bolt actually leaves the rifle. So the safe unload and the strip use different safety positions on purpose. The white dot is the tell — dot showing means the trigger mechanism is locked.
steps.quote: 2. Shift the safety to its "Off" position.
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, p.10

steps.title: Bolt catch depressed, bolt out
steps.action: With the bolt open, depress the bolt catch and pull the bolt out of the gun. Draw it straight back and out; do not lever the rear of the bolt upward.
steps.prose: The 457 uses a dedicated bolt-release controller rather than the 455's trigger, which is one of the features CZ lists for this rifle and the single most important difference to hold in mind if you have both. The bolt handle rotation is only 60 degrees on a 457, so the bolt comes back further per unit of handle movement than on an older rimfire and can surprise you on the way out. Support it as it clears; the extractor and the small rimfire firing pin at the front are the parts you least want dropped on a concrete floor.
steps.quote: 3. Open the bolt, and depressing the bolt catch (Fig.10) and pull the bolt out of the gun.
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 3, p.10

steps.title: Check the stock screws to 3.5 Nm while you are in there
steps.action: With the bolt out, check the tightening of the stock fixing screws — positions 73 and 74 in the parts list — and tighten them as necessary to 3.5 Nm.
steps.prose: CZ prints this as part of the strip rather than as an accessory note, and on a rifle whose wooden stocks are bedded for accuracy it is the maintenance item that quietly decides whether the group opens up. Torque, not feel: 3.5 Nm is a light setting and a screwdriver leaned on will exceed it easily, crushing bedding or splitting a stock. If you have no torque driver, snug and leave it rather than guessing high. This is also the number that differs from the CZ 455's, which takes 3 Nm on the same screws.
steps.quote: Check tightening of the stock fixing screws (pos. 73 and 74) and tighten them as necessary with the torque of 3.5 Nm.
steps.cite: CZ 457 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, closing note, p.10

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrelled action in the stock, bolt out in your hand, magazine or single-shot adapter set aside. That is the whole field strip CZ publishes for the CZ 457 — the barrel stays in the receiver, the trigger mechanism stays fitted, and the bolt does not come apart.
steps.prose: Those pieces reach everything the cleaning section asks for: the barrel and chamber from the breech end with the bolt out of the way, the bolt body and its extractor, the raceway inside the receiver, and the magazine well. CZ closes the strip by saying nothing further is needed for routine maintenance and that after a great many rounds the BOLT goes to a gunsmith for cleaning rather than being opened at home. The caution under it is explicit about not stripping the rifle further.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Do not strip your firearm any further. If you assume that your firearm requires adjustment or repair, entrust this work to a competent gunsmith in a specialized workshop!

deepAbsentReason: CZ's CZ 457 manual publishes nothing past the three-step field strip. Its closing note reads "No further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. When a great number of cartridges has been fired it is advisable to hand the gun to a competent gunsmith for cleaning of the bolt" (p.10) — so the bolt strip, which the CZ 600 book does publish for its own rifle, is expressly handed to a gunsmith here and NO procedure for it is printed. The CAUTION immediately below repeats "Do not strip your firearm any further." The only other operations in the book are trigger pull and travel adjustment, sight adjustment, scope mounting and barrel changing — and the barrel change is bounded too: CZ's own mini-set leaflet states each exchangeable barrel must be fitted individually by a gunsmith before its first use. There is therefore no second-level owner procedure in this manual to walk.

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean patch on the rod through barrel and cartridge chamber, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean — enough on its own if the 457 has fired only a few rounds
For a very dirty barrel, apply gun cleaning solution with a brush, let it act about 10 minutes, then scrub the barrel out thoroughly
Rod and brush enter from the CHAMBER end and the brush is pushed all the way through before reversing; reversing inside the bore sticks the brush
Go gently in a MATCH chamber such as the Varmint MTR's — it is cut to the minimum the CIP standard allows and is less forgiving of a tight brush than a standard chamber
Dry barrel and chamber with a clean patch and check every trace of powder residue and fouling has been removed

cleaning.name: BOLT, RACEWAY & MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the bolt body, its extractor and the bolt face with a dry cloth, old toothbrush, copper bristle brush or wooden scraper — rimfire lubricant and wax carry a lot of grit onto a bolt face
Clean the raceway inside the receiver and the bolt catch recess
Never use the agent designed for barrel bore cleaning on these parts; it stays in the joints and causes corrosion later
Wipe the magazine body and follower, or the single-shot adapter, and leave them dry
Check that no cloth particles or brush bristles have lodged in any part of the rifle

cleaning.name: STOCK & SCREWS
tasks: Maintain the stock with a dry cloth or a furniture-polishing product — that is CZ's own instruction for the wood
Check the stock fixing screws at positions 73 and 74 and set them to 3.5 Nm; on a bedded wooden 457 this is what holds the group together
Look at the bedding while the screws are being checked, and confirm the forend is not bearing hard against the barrel

cleaning.name: PRESERVING
tasks: With barrel, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or apply it as a spray, then remove all excess
At very low temperatures remove the oil from all accessible parts or apply a lubricant made especially for those conditions
Thick preserving grease is for long-term storage in severe climates only and comes off every part thoroughly before use
Pull a dry patch through the barrel before shooting

reassembly: Bolt back into the receiver with the handle raised, pushed forward until it seats, then rotate the handle down — the 457's rotation is only 60 degrees, so the handle travels less than an older rimfire's.
Reinsert the magazine, or the single-shot adapter, until the front catch holds it.
Confirm the stock fixing screws are at 3.5 Nm before the rifle is fired, not after.
Check the trigger adjustment is still safe on the UNLOADED rifle by opening and closing the bolt repeatedly and moving the safety on and off safe; the rifle must not discharge during this check.
Pull a dry patch through the barrel before shooting.
fncheck: Magazine or single-shot adapter out and chamber confirmed empty. Push the safety back to Safety-On and confirm the white dot is uncovered and the trigger will not move; the bolt should still be withdrawable with the safety on, which is by design on this rifle. Check the cocking indicator by sight and touch — its rear part should protrude over the plug when the striker is cocked and drop back when released. Then run CZ's own safety check on the unloaded rifle: open and close the bolt repeatedly and move the safety on and off safe, and confirm the rifle does not discharge at any point. Finish by confirming the stock fixing screws are at 3.5 Nm and the forend is not touching the barrel.
